findings.committee: Education, Young People  and the Welsh Language Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: Adult and Community Learning service costs exceed franchise and grant income, generating £67k deficit
findings.detail: Expected franchise income and grant revenue are insufficient to cover operating costs of the service, creating a £67k year-end budget variance (forecasted £71k).
findings.matters: A non-statutory service unable to achieve cost recovery from projected income indicates either income assumptions are optimistic or the service model is uneconomic
findings.quote: Expected franchise income and grants not covering cost of running service.

findings.committee: Education, Young People  and the Welsh Language Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: Music services planned efficiency saving of £35k has not been achieved and income covers only part of costs
findings.detail: The council budgeted for a £35k efficiency saving in prior-year staffing costs, but this has not materialised. Service level agreement and concert income fall £30k short of covering the staffing costs including agency and travel.
findings.matters: Planned savings that do not materialise suggest budget forecasting includes unachievable assumptions, creating risk of recurring budget pressures
findings.figures: Planned efficiency saving not progressed: £35k; income shortfall: £30k; actual variance: £53k overspend
findings.quote: Income from the SLA & concert revenue does not cover the staffing costs including agency & travel £30k, along with previous year efficiency relating to reduced staffing costs £35k has not progressed.

findings.committee: Education, Young People  and the Welsh Language Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: School meals service lost £562k due to combined income shortfall and cost pressures
findings.detail: Secondary school meal income fell £164k short, snow-related school closures in January cost £89k in lost income, and primary breakfast contributions fell £106k below budget. Simultaneously, repair and maintenance costs increased £122k and staffing and food costs rose £81k across all schools.
findings.matters: A council-operated service experiencing both income loss and cost inflation simultaneously raises questions about pricing adequacy and demand sustainability
findings.figures: Secondary income shortfall £164k; snow closure impact £89k; breakfast income £106k below target; repair/maintenance cost increase £122k; staffing and food cost increase £81k; total variance £562k
findings.quote: Income below target for secondary schools £164k. Reduced 'take up' and loss of income during days schools have been closed following snow in January has reduced the level of income achieved £89k. Primary breakfast voluntary income contributions for care element shortfall £106k. Increased repair & maintenance costs £122k, along with increased staffing & food costs in delivering the service across all schools £81k.

findings.committee: Education, Young People  and the Welsh Language Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: School meals price increase of 7% did not deliver planned £250k saving due to closure days
findings.detail: The 2025/26 budget planned £250k savings from a 7% increase in meal prices. The council reports: 'Actual income failed to match the income target - loss of income during days schools have been closed following snow in January has reduced the level of income achieved.' This was the only reported 2025/26 policy savings shortfall.
findings.matters: Income assumptions underpinning the budget depend on school opening continuity; external events (weather closures) create volatility in expected revenue streams that the council cannot control.
findings.figures: £250k shortfall on 7% meal price increase, loss due to snow closure days
findings.quote: Actual income failed to match the income target - loss of income during days schools have been closed following snow in January has reduced the level of income achieved

findings.committee: Education, Young People  and the Welsh Language Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: School music service has overspent for two consecutive years (£87k in 2024/25, £53k in 2025/26) with 2024/25 savings target still undelivered
findings.detail: A planned £35k saving for 2024/25 was not achieved. The service has subsequently overspent: 'Music Services for Schools were £87k overspent in 2024/25 and were £53k overspent in 2025/26.' The council proposes cost reduction through staffing review and vacant position freezes.
findings.matters: Multi-year consecutive overspends on a specific service indicate cost control failure and carry forward unresolved budget problems that may recur if staffing actions are delayed or ineffective.
findings.quote: Music Services for Schools were £87k overspent in 2024/25 and were £53k overspent in 2025/26
